transcript: The other night, I attended The Lonely Few, a new musical at MCC following a small town rock band and a queer love story. You're made to feel like you're at Paul's Juke Joint, the venue where The Lonely Few perform, and there's some nontraditional on-stage seating for a more immersive feel. I was on a bar stool and was quite close to the actors at multiple points during the show. The story is pretty simple: it's a bit of a will they won't they between the two main characters who both seek new beginnings but have different circumstances holding them back. The plot moves quickly, honestly a little too quickly sometimes, but the focus of this piece is clearly the music which I think does a good job of providing storytelling and entertainment— is a rock concert after all. The score by Zoe Sarnak is one of my favorite new scores I've heard in awhile and the performances by this small but mighty cast are fantastic. Lauren Patten and Taylor Iman Jones really get to rip the roof off in this piece and the sound design is appropriately loud. There were a few times where it was hard to make out all the lyrics but this could have just been from where I was sitting and I wouldn't say that impacted my enjoyment of the show at all. I would love a cast recording but specifically during a performance as opposed to in the studio. I think capturing the live performance energy and messiness would be really special. With that, another program for my collection.
reasoning: Creator is enthusiastic about the score and performances, calling it one of their favorite new scores in a while, with only minor caveats about pacing and lyric clarity. Lands at the top of Positive/bottom of Rave.
